newsitem.title: BURUNDI: U.N. envoy Mohamed Sahnoun arrives in Bujumbura.
newsitem.headline: U.N. envoy Mohamed Sahnoun arrives in Bujumbura.

text.p: Mohamed Sahnoun, the new U.N. and Organisation of African Unity (OAU) special envoy to the Great Lakes region, arrived in Burundi on Thursday on his first visit.
U.N. officials said Sahnouns trip to the capital Bujumbura was essentially an information gathering visit but he would meet military ruler Pierre Buyoya on Friday and other officials.

Sahnoun, the first joint envoy of the United Nations and the OAU, arrived in Africa on Tuesday at his Nairobi headquarters for a mission to bring peace to the region that includes Zaire, Burundi and Rwanda.

Sahnoun has spoken of the need for a comprehensive solution to the Great Lakes crises. But U.N. officials say he will need to tackle problems one by one before conditions are suitable for an overall resolution.

Sahnoun resigned as special representative to Somalia in 1992 after then U.N. secretary-general Boutros Boutros-Ghali rebuked him for saying the U.N. was slow to react to famine in the Horn of Africa country.
Burundi has been under an economic and transport embargo imposed by regional states since shortly after Buyoya and the Tutsi-dominated army seized power last July.
